transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-09
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Jessa Martinez (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (PulseGrid CTO), Elena Varga (Platform Eng Lead), Marcus Li (Security Architect), Priya Shah (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to align on Helm operator behavior for hybrid deployments, KMS/HSM integration requirements for marketplace listing, and UAT/canary schedule. Action items captured.

[00:00] Jessa Martinez: Okay good morning everyone, thanks for carving out time. we wanted to focus on two things today — helm operator compatibility for your hybrid clusters and the KMS/HSM constraints for the private deployment path and marketplace listing.
[00:22] Rajiv Menon: Yep that's right. We're planning a hybrid topology: managed cloud nodes plus on-prem edge racks. main ask is: can Redwood's helm package handle the nodeAffinity and PV semantics we use? also need to validate KMS integration for secrets.
[00:38] Omar Patel: Absolutely. quick note: our current helm chart has optional nodeSelector and toleration blocks, but the operator we ship as an opt-in CRD does some lifecycle hooks that assume CSI volumes behave a certain way. we had customers in the past where reclaimPolicy was mismatch and it caused pods to hang on terminate.
[00:55] Elena Varga: yeah that's one of our pain points — our on-prem PVs use NFS with retain policy and cloud side uses gp3. we need the install to not change PV reclaimPolicy.
[01:14] Omar Patel: Understood. we can add a values switch to skip PV provisioning for certain node pools, and make the post-install hook idempotent. i'll flag that as an action.
[01:29] Marcus Li: on KMS — our security team requires that encryption keys for inference logs and any customer prompt metadata be stored in our HSM managed by Thales. does Redwood support external KMS with HSM-backed keys and key rotation policies?
[01:46] Lina Cho: Yes, we do support external KMS integrations. in our private deployment flow we integrate with a customer's KMS via a connector. caveat: we need the service account in your VPC to be able to reach the HSM endpoint; if it's air-gapped we'll need a proxy. also, we currently support KMIP and cloud KMS APIs; if Thales uses a custom API we can map it but it'll be an engineering spike.
[02:12] Rajiv Menon: it is Thales with KMIP, but our firewall restricts outbound. we can open specific IP ranges. i'll share that.
[02:21] Jessa Martinez: quick housekeeping — we'll add a section in the marketplace listing about KMS compatibility and on-prem HSM notes. Lina will assemble the compatibility matrix.
[02:35] [00:03:00] Omar Patel: thinking about the operator itself — right now the CRD creates a StatefulSet for model workers and a Deployment for the controller. in hybrid mode we support nodeSelector partitioning but we do not auto-migrate KV cache across nodes. that means if you want to colocate GPUs on cloud nodes and inference bridging on-prem, there are considerations for latency on cold starts.
[03:06] Elena Varga: can you explain the KV cache piece again? sometimes the docs mention "K-V cache" and sometimes "K V cache" in our internal notes — it's a bit inconsistent.
[03:20] Omar Patel: haha yes transcription artifacts aside, the KV cache is per-worker and stored in memory with optional persistence to local NVMe. in a hybrid deployment the best practice is to pin warm workers to the cloud GPU nodes and use a fast interconnect or a small regional cache for on-prem. we can also enable prefix caching at the API gateway layer to reduce cold token cost.
[03:45] Priya Shah: are there additional network ports for the operator or runtime we need to open? our security team hates surprise ports.
[03:52] Lina Cho: we'll provide a short list. controller to workers uses gRPC on 8200 by default; metrics are on 9090, and health probes on 8081. for KMS we talk to HTTPS endpoints outbound. if you want private connectivity we can wire a VPC peering or a proxy, or ship a small local connector that talks to the HSM over KMIP.
[04:17] Rajiv Menon: for marketplace listing, we need a clearly documented network and IAM requirements. procurement will not accept vague wording.
[04:25] Jessa Martinez: noted — Lina will prepare a "hard requirements" section for the listing.
[04:31] [00:10:00] Omar Patel: another gotcha we've seen: helm hooks that create cluster-scoped RBAC can fail in restricted clusters. we'll add an option to install via a namespaced mode where clusterRoleBindings are precreated by an admin job or sequence. this is especially important for air-gapped or flagged clusters.
[04:55] Marcus Li: clusterRoleBindings are not allowed by our compliance team without a control review. can the installer emit a manifest you can apply with RBAC after review?
[05:03] Omar Patel: yes we can produce a rbac-manifests/ directory in the chart that you apply during procurement checks. we'll also include a validation script that does no live changes, just a dry-run.
[05:16] Elena Varga: about the helm chart values — please include explicit notes for maxReplica and batchSize defaults. our workloads are bursty and default batch sizes caused timeouts in some tests.
[05:27] Lina Cho: good call, we'll add guidance and recommended values for bursty workloads and a sample values-staging.yaml.
[05:33] [00:20:00] Jessa Martinez: switching to marketplace packaging — there are two parallel goals: 1) get a listing that customers can deploy via marketplace with a one-click install for supported cloud, and 2) provide a downloadable helm chart for our partners to run in private/on-prem. the listing needs the compatibility matrix, support & SLA wording, and a walkthrough for KMS setup.
[06:01] Rajiv Menon: on the SLA piece — we need clear statements about what Redwood manages for marketplace vs what we manage on-prem. for the private deployment we want Redwood to leave the control plane bits but not have any secret access — i.e., no plaintext keys in Redwood control plane.
[06:18] Lina Cho: that is standard for our Private deployment: keys remain in customer KMS and Redwood stores only references/aliases. for hosted offer, we have a different flow which we won't use. we'll make that explicit in the listing copy.
[06:30] Priya Shah: is there a way to verify that the model logs we store in S3 are encrypted with the right key without Redwood decrypting them? we need evidence for audits.
[06:42] Omar Patel: yes we can provide encryption-at-rest proofs: S3 object metadata with key ID, and an audit log entry for each write that includes the KMS key alias. we can include verification scripts in the deployment repo.
[06:57] [00:30:00] Rajiv Menon: timeline question: procurement wants a pilot in 2 weeks, but we have internal compliance gating that might push to 3. what's a realistic earliest canary?
[07:07] Jessa Martinez: if we can get the staging kubeconfig and KMS access info in the next week, our SEs can run a constrained canary on 2026-11-20. that's the date we proposed.
[07:17] Elena Varga: ok we'll try for 11/18 to hand over the kubeconfig and a scoped service account.
[07:22] Marcus Li: make sure the service account doesn't have permissions for other workloads. we prefer least privilege.
[07:26] Lina Cho: we'll produce a recommended RBAC manifest for the service account scoped to the namespaces used by the canary.
[07:33] [00:40:00] Omar Patel: quick demo note — when we do the canary we'll stream logs into a temporary observability workspace and show token-level cost breakdown and KV cache hit metrics. that helps validate cost estimates.
[07:49] Priya Shah: is the observability workspace multi-tenant? our security team is concerned about cross-tenant leakage.
[07:55] Lina Cho: for canary runs we'll use an isolated workspace; logs are segmented and you'll get a retention-limited view. for production we'll recommend a dedicated workspace or a private deployment.
[08:08] Rajiv Menon: any blockers on RBAC for marketplace listing?
[08:12] Omar Patel: none technical, just we need to make the cluster-scoped parts optional and provide the preapply manifests for locked-down installations.
[08:21] [00:58:00] Jessa Martinez: okay let's walk through action items quickly. Omar will change the helm hooks and add values skipPV and namespacedInstall flag. Lina will draft the compatibility matrix and marketplace notes. Elena will share KMS/HSM IP ranges and policies. Priya will prepare the staging service account. Rajiv will coordinate procurement timeline.
[08:41] Rajiv Menon: sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[08:48] Marcus Li: one more security callout — rotation window for keys needs to be at most 90 days per our policy; can Redwood handle key rotation events without interrupting live inference? we had a bad outage once when a rotation forced re-encryption.
[08:59] Omar Patel: the runtime supports key aliasing — we fetch by alias and refresh on rotation. there is a short window for cache rewarm, but we built a small fallback that keeps serving on a previous alias until new streams are primed. we'll test rotation during the canary.
[09:16] Jessa Martinez: great. i'll follow up with a short email summarizing the next steps and attach the PRs/docs once ready.
[09:22] [01:15:00] Closing: informal wrap up and thanks.

Recap / Next steps (auto):
